custom_soc.executive_summary: Custom silicon acceleration for AI workloads has shifted from niche to competitive necessity: Google TPUs now distribute via Oracle OCI, Amazon pursues Decart ($7B) to escape NVIDIA inference costs, AWS launches TorchNeuron to erode CUDA lock-in, and Google-led custom chips forecast to outship GPUs by 2028. The interface value has migrated from monolithic GPU dominance to heterogeneous chiplet/HBM stacks with software abstraction layers (PyTorch, Bedrock prompt caching) that decouple workload optimization from hardware vendor.

packaging.executive_summary: Packaging competitive topology pivots toward geographic supply-chain redundancy and material-layer control rather than node-driven consolidation. Hanmi Semiconductor's U.S. base opening, Amkor's margin gains in advanced packaging, and Intel-AMD chiplet collaboration signals fragment design-at-interface arbitrage further; simultaneously, adhesive localization (Henkel Korea) and interposer heterogeneity (Egis-SiPearl CPU chiplets for Europe) erode single-vendor packaging dominance and raise barriers to technical lock-in at the substrate-protocol boundary.

cpo_optics.executive_summary: Co-packaged optics (CPO) and silicon photonics are consolidating as critical AI infrastructure interfaces. Nvidia-SPIL's 15x capacity expansion by mid-2027 and Taiwan's LandMark's record Q3 EPS on silicon photonics demand confirm supply-chain lock-in at the optical-electronic boundary; Micro LED variants (Erised, Starksemi, San'an backing) now passing customer validation, signaling technology divergence at the modulation layer. Market estimates of $50B+ reflect mainstream adoption, but competitive pressure concentrates around transceiver density and thermal management at the package edge.
